micro_lessons.title: Food Diversity and Changing Food Practices

foundation.concept_text: People in different regions eat different types of food based on crops grown and traditions.

standard.concept_text: Traditional food varies across India due to climate, soil type, locally grown crops and cultural practices.

advanced.concept_text: Food diversity reflects agricultural patterns, ecological conditions and socio-cultural evolution over time.

foundation.concept_text: Carbohydrates and fats give us energy. Proteins help us grow.

standard.concept_text: Carbohydrates provide instant energy, fats store energy, and proteins help in growth and repair of the body.

advanced.concept_text: Nutrients perform distinct physiological roles including metabolic energy release, tissue repair and structural development.

videos.title: Understanding Nutrients in Food
videos.instructional_purpose: Explain role of carbohydrates, fats and proteins

foundation.concept_text: Vitamins and minerals protect our body from diseases.

standard.concept_text: Deficiency of vitamins and minerals can cause diseases such as scurvy, rickets, goitre and anaemia.

advanced.concept_text: Protective nutrients regulate physiological processes and prevent systemic disorders caused by long-term deficiencies.

images.title: Iodised Salt Packet
images.instructional_purpose: Connect mineral supplementation to daily life

foundation.concept_text: We can test some nutrients like starch, fat and protein using simple experiments.

standard.concept_text: Iodine test detects starch, oily patch test detects fats and copper sulphate test detects proteins.

advanced.concept_text: Chemical reactions causing colour changes help identify the presence of specific macronutrients in food samples.

videos.title: How to Test Nutrients in Food

micro_lessons.title: Balanced Diet, Millets and Food Miles

foundation.concept_text: A balanced diet contains all nutrients, roughage and water in the right amount.

standard.concept_text: Millets are nutrition-rich cereals and junk foods contain high sugar and fat but low nutrients.

advanced.concept_text: Sustainable food choices, reduced food miles and nutrient-dense diets contribute to long-term health and environmental balance.
